title: The Walkthrough: choose the page structure
question: The world is settled; this is composition. Lock one structure for /walkthrough, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: The booking desk
options.thesis: The calendar sits in the first viewport, on a corner of the owner's desk in miniature.
materials: report card with a canary 'Where I'd start' row
options.viewport: Offer, pitch-free promise and report contents at left; the live Cal calendar at right on a miniature desk with the canary; steps start below.
options.risk: Asks for the booking before a cold visitor has read why; the Cal iframe owns the look of the dominant object.

options.label: A letter from me
options.thesis: The page reads as one letter from Nick, with the report as its enclosure.
materials: miniature report booklet with pill-tag tabs
options.viewport: A tall white letter carries the offer in my voice, signed and with the booking button; the report booklet sits in the right margin.
options.risk: Long first-person copy can read slower than a scanner wants, and a sheet-on-desk frame drifts toward editorial cliché if the enclosure goes quiet.

options.label: Fair questions
options.thesis: The page is organized by the questions an owner asks before booking, answered in order.
options.viewport: Offer and booking button at left; a four-row question index at right (What do I get? Is it a pitch? Is it really free? Is it a fit?).
options.risk: Four thumbnails can turn into an icon grid; the questions must stay the hero, not the pictures.
